title: Dave Canales previews Packers matchup: 'We have to recapture our process'
headline: Panthers enter a short week against the Packers with Damien Lewis and a corner (likely Akayleb Evans, 'AK') day to day; no one is ruled out yet, and testing on Tuesday decides availability.
summary: Canales framed Thursday night at Lambeau as another championship opportunity. He praised the Packers as an explosive offense that also leads the NFL in turnovers. He said several injured players are day to day and that tomorrow brings heavy testing to see whether they can move and do their jobs. No one has been ruled out yet. Because of the injuries he is weighing backups by game-plan fit instead of picking the most obvious replacement. He named Jake Curhan and Corey Bullock as offensive line options, and Marco Wilson as a quicker corner option if AK can't go. The rest of the session was about refocusing after a bad loss: recapturing their process, fundamentals, and ball security. He also talked about stopping the run and tackling Josh Jacobs, who returns for Green Bay, and expects the Packers to run the ball after seeing the Panthers give up about 250 rushing yards. Carolina's own offensive plans got almost no discussion.

injuries.detail: Did not practice Tuesday and is day to day. He will be tested tomorrow to see if he can move and do his job. Canales has not ruled anyone out.
Did not practice and is day to day. The coach refers to him as 'AK' and the transcript misspells him as 'Caleb Evans'. He will be tested tomorrow.

signals.claim: Jake Curhan could step in on the offensive line if a starter can't go on Thursday.
signals.note: Offensive line depth is thin, and the run game's quality depends on who fills in for the injured linemen.
signals.quote: who's played quality ball for us and we've won games with Jake

signals.claim: Corey Bullock is an offensive line option if a lineman is out Thursday.
signals.note: He is a fill-in candidate along the line, so Carolina's run-blocking could change if he plays.

signals.claim: Marco Wilson could start or take extra snaps at corner if Akayleb Evans can't play.
signals.note: He is a depth corner who could see a bigger role against Green Bay's pass-heavy offense.
signals.quote: Marco Wilson's a quicker athletic mover

topics.detail: Josh Jacobs returns for Green Bay. Canales expects similar run schemes, stresses team tackling and leverage, and notes that Jacobs can also hurt them as a receiver out of the backfield.

Carolina allowed about 250 rushing yards last game, and Canales expects Green Bay to try to run on them. He also expects Jordan Love to throw deep, since the Packers have the league's highest pass rate.
The focus is on recapturing their process, fundamentals, ball security, alignments, and special teams coverage after a tough division loss. Canales said the team is 'humbled'.
Day-to-day injured players will be tested tomorrow, and the team is preparing both the possible returners and the backups.

title: Matt LaFleur on the Panthers: 'We've got a great challenge ahead of us'
headline: Josh Jacobs is working back from rust, Savion Williams is a rising downfield target, and the O-line is thin: Glover is hurt, Rhyan's IR status is undecided, and Zeitler is ready if needed for Thursday at Carolina.
summary: LaFleur used a short-week Tuesday session to preview Thursday night's game against the Panthers. He praised John Williams for stepping in for the first time, but he wouldn't commit to Williams starting Thursday. Sean Rhyan's possible move to IR is undecided, and Travis Glover, who played every snap and hurt his knee, missed practice and is only 'hopeful' for Thursday. Kevin Zeitler is ready to play if needed, with no rush to force him in. Josh Jacobs was described as shaking off rust. LaFleur blamed the weak run numbers on the whole offense (play calls, leverage, bad looks) rather than on Jacobs. Savion Williams was singled out for providing a spark on third downs and was told to 'be the goon,' and Kaleb Johnson's game-day role is tied to special teams and pass protection. Zaire Franklin will miss another game. LaFleur was upbeat but guarded about the pass-rush unit and penalties, and about the Micah Parsons timeline ('there's a chance' he practices next week). He called Carolina a dangerous, motivated team led by a well-playing Bryce Young.

injuries.detail: Reporter asked if he's headed to IR; LaFleur said there's still time before they decide.
Knee injury discovered the morning after the game (he played every snap). Not able to practice Tuesday; LaFleur is hopeful for Thursday but still working through it.
Will be out again on the short week.
Has not played yet this season after joining without an offseason or camp; gradually working back in and ready if needed.
Asked about him as 'Mica'. LaFleur hopes he starts practicing next week and said 'there's a chance,' but it is up to the medical staff.

signals.note: Impressed in his first action, but LaFleur wouldn't confirm he starts Thursday; the line is still being sorted.
signals.quote: Pretty impressive to be able to go in there the first time

signals.note: LaFleur backs the rookie CB after a tough penalty and says he has the mentality to bounce back; no role change implied.
signals.quote: He's definitely wired the right way.

signals.claim: Rhyan's IR decision will be made in the coming days.
signals.note: Another interior O-line loss could affect the run game and pass protection.
signals.quote: we got some time yet before we determine that

signals.claim: Glover is hopeful to play Thursday after missing Tuesday's practice.
signals.note: A tackle injury on a short week threatens O-line stability for both the run and pass games.

signals.claim: Zeitler will play Thursday if the team needs him.
signals.note: He's a ready fill-in for injured linemen and a possible lift for the offense.
signals.quote: I think if we need him. Absolutely. I feel confident with him.

signals.claim: Jacobs remains the lead back; touches may be play-dependent in his second game back.
signals.note: LaFleur praised his physicality and blamed the weak run numbers (11 carries) on the whole offense; the matchup against a Carolina defense that stops the run is a concern.
signals.quote: I loved how he brought a lot of just physicality toughness.

signals.claim: Johnson's game-day opportunities depend on special teams contributions and pass protection.
signals.note: He's not the starter and has work to do to earn a role, so he's a low-confidence fantasy bench option.
signals.quote: making sure that we're, we're rock solid on some of the pass protection stuff

signals.claim: Williams will keep a physical downfield and third-down role in the passing game.
signals.note: He has made plays on multiple third downs the last two weeks; LaFleur wants more of his size and physicality.
signals.quote: He's a big guy that is physical and we need that from him.

signals.note: The linebacker is unavailable on a short week.
He wore the green dot (defensive play-caller) and LaFleur praised how he handled it.
signals.quote: I thought he did a really good job.

topics.detail: Thursday night at Carolina. LaFleur called them a motivated, dangerous team coming off a turnover-filled loss. He noted Bryce Young is playing well, the Panthers have plenty of weapons and a good line, and their tough defense, run by Ejiro Evero, has been hit with injuries.

LaFleur said run-game struggles fall on everyone: play calls, line play, tight ends and receivers. He cited breakdowns, missed targets and bad looks. Carolina's defense commits to stopping the run, so patience and consistency from all 11 are needed.

LaFleur said the pass rush has had good moments but needs to grow. He stressed teaching a 'strike zone' to avoid roughing-the-passer penalties and praised Karl Brooks for avoiding landing on the QB with body weight.

LaFleur described how teams submit clips to the league office and get a yes/no response. He called officiating hard, wants consistency, and said it mostly helps with player education. He said he's moving on from the frustrations after Thursday's loss.
The hook-and-ladder with Matthew Golden and MarShawn Lloyd didn't work as hoped, but it still gained positive yardage. LaFleur called it a play seen around the league in longer-yardage situations.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 26, 2026
headline: Saquon Barkley played through a back tweak on a pitch count in the loss to Dallas and was productive, but he saw fewer snaps than planned; the Eagles' run defense and pass rush remain concerns.
summary: Sirianni recapped the Monday night loss to the Cowboys by blaming himself and the staff for the run defense, citing poor block destruction, missed tackles, and a lack of execution. He said Dallas stayed ahead of the sticks, ran play action well, and kept the defense off balance, and he did not pin the season-long lack of pass-rush pressure on a single cause. Saquon Barkley played on a pitch count after a back issue, was monitored constantly, came out early in the second half, and ended up with fewer snaps than the team initially planned. Sirianni praised Barkley's toughness and said he was productive whenever he touched the ball, including a 29-yard run. He acknowledged that six day-one starters were down on offense by the end of the game, but called it life in the NFL and refused to use it as an excuse. He said early offensive success came from an efficient run game, tempo calls, run/play-action, explosives in the run game, red-zone finishing, and third-down conversions of just over 40%. He also talked about developing leadership with younger players, staying the same version of yourself, and called the division wide open with ten games left.

injuries.detail: Tweaked his back on his first run, a 29-yarder. He played on a pitch count, came out early in the second half, and played less than initially planned. Sirianni said the doctors and trainers felt he was ready to go.
A reporter cited Lane Johnson's injury as part of lost locker-room leadership. Sirianni did not give a status.

signals.claim: Barkley's snaps were managed on a pitch count against Dallas and ended up lower than the team initially planned.
signals.note: Barkley is productive but his workload is tied to his back health, so monitor his practice status and snap count for next week.
signals.quote: he definitely played a little less than what we initially thought

topics.detail: Sirianni took responsibility for giving up a lot of rushing yards and cited block destruction, tackling, and positioning. He said the team reviews every missed tackle and works on fixes in practice.

Asked about weak pressure rates all season, he said there is no single cause and the team will look at common themes. Dallas stayed in manageable third downs and used play action to keep the defense off balance.
Six day-one offensive starters were down by the end of the game. Sirianni called it part of the NFL and stressed developing depth without making excuses.
Early success came from run efficiency, tempo calls, run/play-action, explosive runs, red-zone finishing, and third-down conversion of just over 40%. He wants better on third down.

He urged the team to stay the same version of itself, compared this stretch to the 2021 finish that propelled the franchise, and said Barkley spoke to the team. He called the division wide open with ten games left.
